doc.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Soundtracks and Music for the Fifth World
title: Recording Fifth World with Living Colour's Will Calhoun
summary: Two guitars and two drummers, chants with Joan Henry and Denis Yerry, and a drum duel at the end.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Yeah, Corey. The bassist was… We’ll get that.
Did he play on this? Was he on this project?
Because you had Lonnie playing bass on this project.

Well Lonnie was on bass but we had two guitarists and two drummers. Will Calhoun… We were big Living Colour fans so I had this idea to have two guitars and two drums on this. Will and I… I went up to Will’s and we rehearsed. I played keyboard with him. We’d come up with how we would play the “Fifth World” and he worked out his part that worked with mine. It was great, it was so much fun. Joan Henry worked with the vocals, the singing. We also had a big ceremonial drum that’s upstairs and we’d also beat on that in 5/4 on the record.
No, we were doing chants. We had a big drum duo/battle with me and Will going at it at the end. Did you ever hear that? You’d love it.
No. I don’t even know the label.

We had that and then Joanie did some sort of round chants. Then I wrote something called “Two Guitar Chant/Dohiyi,” which Joanie wrote some lyrics to for that. Which we co-wrote together. I wrote the arrangements and the melody and she wrote the chant on it. There was someone else singing in on it named Robert…
Robert Rosario. So we had a great crew. Michael Cain is also on that and did a really fantastic job playing keyboards and piano.
So this must have been a very extended project. You’re talking about rehearsals…
